rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it overstates confidence in hatching/herniation and describes possible vacuoles/granularity/fragmentation that are not clearly discernible from this single image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrium, prior cycle history, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from embryo/patient factors to prognosis, though some probability adjustments are somewhat speculative and additive.

Mostly aligned on SET and lifestyle counseling, but includes less-supported suggestions such as ERA/thrombophilia workup after limited failure history, routine estradiol consideration, and PGT-A rationale in a 22-year-old.
Provides clear practical recommendations for current transfer and future planning, though some suggested investigations/interventions may be more aggressive than standard for this scenario.
